answers.how: Measured the yoga ball pixel diameter (171 px at t=0.6s, Z=2.133 m) and calibrated the camera focal length (~722 px) using the prior velocity of 2.5104 m/s and apparent size change across frames.
Measured the soccer ball pixel diameter (82 px at t=0.6s) and converted to cm using its depth of 1.9370 m and the calibrated focal length.
Tracked the 3D trajectories of the soccer ball and basketball to t=2.0s (Frame 48) using pixel coordinates and depth progression, then computed the 3D Euclidean distance between them.
Measured the positions and depths of the basketball (in the foreground at the bottom of Frame 48) and the stationary yoga ball at t=2.0s to compute their 3D separation.
Estimated the vertical height of the soccer ball above the floor plane at t=2.0s from its trajectory after bouncing.
Combined the image-plane velocity components of the soccer ball between Frames 13 and 16 at Z=1.9370 m with the depth velocity component derived from Z(0.6s) and Z(0.9s).
Measured the pixel displacement of the soccer ball around Frame 22 (t=0.917s) at depth Z=1.5850 m and combined with its depth velocity component.
Measured the downward pixel displacement of the basketball between Frames 24 and 29 around t=1.1s at depth Z=2.4200 m and combined with its depth velocity.
Measured the basketball displacement across Frames 36 to 41 around t=1.6s (near the apex of its bounce, Z=1.9015 m) and combined with its forward depth velocity.
